title: Child poverty impact dashboard
subject: How federal and state tax and benefit reforms (Child Tax Credits, EITCs, child allowances, dependent exemptions, SNAP) would change child poverty, household incomes and government budgets in a chosen state. The page has no default reform and no static results: every figure is computed on demand for the reform and state a user picks. The figures pinned here are the dashboard's own scorecard of seven representative reforms for 2026 (analysis/reform_scores/results.json, scored in California or New York) and its Build P audit's California figure for restoring the 2021 Child Tax Credit.
search_terms: state child tax credit child poverty effect
restore 2021 expanded child tax credit California child poverty
Working Parents Tax Relief Act state estimate
California Young Child Tax Credit increase cost
Empire State Child Credit children under 4 $2,000
New York dependent exemption tax expenditure

arpa_ctc_restored.description: The dashboard's 'Restore 2021 expanded CTC' option in 2026: it sets only the ARPA amounts ($3,600 under 6, $3,000 older), full refundability and the ARPA phase-out (frontend/lib/reforms.ts federal_ctc_expanded; gov.irs.credits.ctc.amount.arpa, refundable.fully_refundable, phase_out.arpa.in_effect). With full refundability each child's refundable maximum is the larger of the base and ARPA amounts (ctc_refundable_maximum). The age limit stays at 17: ctc_qualifying_child uses the top threshold of gov.irs.credits.ctc.amount.base, 17 from 2022, so 17-year-olds are not covered, although the option's description says ages 6-17 (policyengine-us at 1.729.5, commit 03b804dd).

arpa_ctc_2021.description: The American Rescue Plan Child Tax Credit design of 2021 as the producers model it: $3,600 per child under 6, $3,000 for children 6 to 17 (17-year-olds included), fully refundable. What each claim measures it against is in its baseline_policy (null: the law in force in the year the producer scores) and its conditions.

child_allowance_3000.description: A federal cash allowance of $3,000 a year for every child under 18 with no income test (gov.contrib.ubi_center.basic_income, three age tiers all at $3,000, cutoff 18), added to 2026 law.

wptra.description: Rep. McDonald Rivet's Working Parents Tax Relief Act from 2026: the federal EITC credit percentage rises for each qualifying child under 4 (42.24 points with one child; 30.07 points per young child, up to 3, with two or more) and the phase-out rate rises 5 points per young child (gov.contrib.congress.mcdonald_rivet.working_parents_tax_relief_act). ITEP describes the same bill as raising the maximum credit by $5,500 per child under 4, for up to 3 children.

ca_yctc_2000.description: California's Young Child Tax Credit maximum raised to $2,000 per return in 2026 (current law $1,189 in 2025, indexed).

ny_escc_under4_2000.description: New York's Empire State Child Credit for children under 4 raised from $1,000 (the 2025 budget's amount for 2025-2027) to $2,000 in 2026.

ca_eitc_100.description: The CalEITC adjustment factor (gov.states.ca.tax.income.credits.earned_income.adjustment.factor) raised from 85% to 100% in 2026.

ny_dependent_exemption_repealed.description: New York's $1,000 personal income tax exemption per dependent (Tax Law section 616) removed in 2026.

provenance.note: results.json records no run time, engine or dataset. score_reforms.py posts each scenario to the deployed Modal endpoint, not the repository pin: analysis/reform_scores/SWEEP.md at the same commit (0525a73) says the deployed endpoint was 'behind the repo pin (1.739.4)', predates 1.731.0, and labels it about 1.729.5 (the pin moved to 1.742.0 on 24 June). results.json's New York dependent-exemption row equals sweep/1.729.5.json's NY:ny_dependent_exemption to every digit, which dates that row; every row has seconds 0, so all seven were written from the same uncommitted cache, and the other six are taken to share the deployment. provenance.dataset: hf://policyengine/policyengine-us-data/states/NY.h5 (per-state calibrated CPS file, loaded without a revision, so the file version is not recoverable; the backend used these files from 2026-05-29, 6bd1bf5, to 2026-07-07, 2d26cac, then a sparse Populace pin, 053baf6c, until Microcosm Build P on 2026-08-20, a4dce6a)
provenance.note: results.json records no run time, engine or dataset. score_reforms.py posts each scenario to the deployed Modal endpoint, not the repository pin: analysis/reform_scores/SWEEP.md at the same commit (0525a73) says the deployed endpoint was 'behind the repo pin (1.739.4)', predates 1.731.0, and labels it about 1.729.5 (the pin moved to 1.742.0 on 24 June). results.json's New York dependent-exemption row equals sweep/1.729.5.json's NY:ny_dependent_exemption to every digit, which dates that row; every row has seconds 0, so all seven were written from the same uncommitted cache, and the other six are taken to share the deployment. The engine is therefore that deployment, version not recorded, about 1.729.5. computed_at is the commit time of the file. The dashboard's About page says results predating its August 2026 dataset switch are not comparable with what the live page computes.
